sources.excerpt: MXR® SUB MACHINE® FUZZ - Dunlop Toggle menu Compare --> Register I Sign in Search Bag Search Close Products --> All Products --> --> Electronics MXR Cry Baby Way Huge Dunlop Electronics Authentic Hendrix Pedal Parts Electronic Parts Legacy Products Guitar Picks Tortex Nylon Max-Grip Jazz Herco Gator Grip Celluloid Ultex Primetone Delrin 500 Flow Finger & Thumb Stubby Variety Packs Artist Series Graphic Artist Series Pick Tins Other Clearance Accessories Capos Slides & Tonebars MXR Cables Care & Maintenance Strap Retainer Straps Tuners Pick Holders GrooveTech Tools Accu-Fret Fretwire Clearance Strings Artist Series Electric Bass Acoustic Classical Americana Ukulele Apparel Shirts Hoodies Hats Artists Lifestyle Sign in MXR® SUB MACHINE® FUZZ M225 Description *LEGACY PRODUCT / NO LONGER IN PRODUCTION   The Sub Machine Fuzz combines shaggy fuzz with a growling sub octave circuit—switchable between series and parallel modes—with an octave up fuzz mode for searing subterannean sounds.   This pedal can be powered by a 9-volt battery, a Dunlop ECB003 9-volt adapter, or the DC Brick™, Iso-Brick™, and Mini Iso-Brick™ power supplies (not included). Warranty Information The Long Story The Sub Machine Fuzz kicks open the door to epic and unbridled sonic exploration. This mean little box combines the shaggy vintage tones of the La Machine Fuzz with a growling sub octave circuit, giving you a one way ticket to the sonic frontiers of heavy. The Sub Machine Fuzz features the La Machine Fuzz's circuitry and all of its functions—from its Volume, Tone, and Fuzz controls to its electrifying octave up mode.—but it's also got an old school sub octave circuit with its own level control, so you can dial in just the right mix of fuzz and sub octave signals. To further broaden the Sub Machine Fuzz's thunderous tonal palette, the MXR team added a Series switch so you can run the sub octave signal straight into the fuzz—for some seriously subterranean saturation—or alongside the fuzz for a split channel effect. You may find the information you need in the FAQs about the MXR SUB MACHINE FUZZ M225 listed below. How can I correct the issue if there's no sound coming from the MXR SUB MACHINE fuzz pedal? Ensure that the input and output cables are connected properly between your guitar and the amplifier. Make sure the BYPASS footswitch is engaged, as indicated by the blue LED light. Also, check that the power supply is connected correctly and the battery is installed if you're using one. 0 What should I do if the fuzz sound is too faint or weak? Rotate the FUZZ control clockwise to increase the amount of fuzz. Additionally, ensure that the VOLUME knob is adjusted properly to increase the overall output of the fuzz signal. 0 How do I switch from Series to Parallel mode on the MXR SUB MACHINE? Use the SERIES switch to toggle between modes. The yellow LED will indicate when the pedal is in Series mode. Ensure the switch is fully engaged to change the processing path of the Sub-Octave and Fuzz signals. 0 Why isn't the Octave Up feature working on my pedal? Ensure that the OCTAVE footswitch is engaged, which will be indicated by the red LED. For optimal Octave Up settings, it is recommended to play above the 10th fret with the neck pickup selected. 0 What could be causing a power issue with my pedal when using a DC adaptor? Check that you are using an appropriate 9-volt AC adapter such as the Dunlop ECB003 or similar. Confirm that the adapter is correctly plugged into both the pedal and a power source. 0 Is the manual of the MXR SUB MACHINE FUZZ M225 available in English?
